title: Carpet Removal and Disposal: What It Costs and What's Included in Sammamish
meta: Carpet removal and disposal is $0.45 per sq ft at Wills Flooring, haul-away included. What a Sammamish tear-out covers, and when ripping it out yourself pays.
keywords: carpet removal cost, carpet removal and disposal Sammamish, how to dispose of old carpet King County, what is included in carpet tear out, remove carpet yourself or hire

blocks.lead: Removing old carpet and pad and hauling it away is $0.45 per sq ft at Wills Flooring, its own line next to installation labor of $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in or $1.29 glue-down, stairs $30 per step.
blocks.detail: That line covers cutting and rolling the old carpet, pulling the pad and every staple, checking the tack strip and taking it all to the transfer station the same day. Scraping glued-down carpet, sealing a pet-soaked subfloor and replacing failed tack strip are extra, quoted once we see them.

blocks.html: A Sammamish carpet job is rarely small. Klahanie, Trossachs and Sahalee homes from the 1990s and 2000s often carry carpet through the whole upstairs, down the main staircase and across a bonus room, and after fifteen years of kids and a golden retriever it all goes at once. The first question we get is whether removal is included, and the second is whether it is cheaper to rip it out yourself first. Both are answered below, along with what the tear-out line actually buys you.

blocks.text: What the $0.45 covers, and what sits outside it

items.title: Square footage and layout
items.text: The rate is flat per square foot, so open rooms and fiddly closets bill the same. That is deliberate: you can work out your own removal line before we arrive.

items.title: Stairs
items.text: Each tread is cut, pried and de-stapled by hand, and stair pad is usually glued or heavily stapled. Stairs are counted per step, not in the floor area, so we list them separately on the quote.

items.title: How it was installed
items.text: Stretch-in over pad is what the $0.45 assumes. Glued-down carpet over a slab has to be scraped and the adhesive residue dealt with, which counts as subfloor prep and is quoted after we look. Double-stick is the slowest of all.

items.title: Condition and weight
items.text: Wet, pet-soaked or moldy pad must be bagged, and the subfloor underneath often needs cleaning or sealing before new pad goes down. The tear-out rate still applies; the sealing is a separate line we price once we see the plywood.

blocks.text: Price your Sammamish tear-out right now

blocks.note: Tick Remove old carpet and pad to add the $0.45 per sq ft tear-out. Carpet and pad are quoted at the estimate.

blocks.html: A real Klahanie job: 1,450 sq ft of bedrooms, hall and bonus room upstairs plus a 14-step staircase. Removal is 1,450 × $0.45 = $653. Installation is 1,450 × $0.99 + 14 × $30 = $1,436 + $420 = $1,856. That is $2,509 of labor on one line-item quote, plus the carpet and pad, quoted at the estimate because the product you pick moves the total more than we do.

items.text: Rooms cleared of small items, closets emptied, pets shut in another room.
items.note: Vacuum first if the carpet is very dirty; it keeps the dust down during cutting.

items.text: Carpet is cut into strips about 3 ft wide, pulled from the tack strip and rolled tight with tape.
items.note: Strips are sized to fit the stairwell and the truck.

items.text: Pad is pulled, bagged if wet, and staples are pulled or driven flush across the whole subfloor.
items.note: This is the slow, unglamorous part.

items.text: Tack strip inspected, squeaks screwed down, soft or stained areas photographed and discussed before new pad goes down.
items.note: Pet stains on the subfloor get an enzyme clean or sealer, quoted separately.

items.text: Everything goes to a licensed transfer station the same day, and new pad and carpet usually start right after.
items.note: Whole upstairs plus stairs: tear-out is usually a morning.

blocks.text: Should you rip it out yourself?

a.title: Do it yourself when
items: It is stretch-in carpet over pad, not glued down
You have a truck or trailer for the King County transfer station, which charges by weight
You are willing to pull every staple, not just the carpet
You want to see the subfloor early, before the estimate

b.title: Hire it out when
items: Carpet is glued down or on stairs
The pad is pet-soaked or moldy; that is a mask-and-bag job
There is a lot of it; a whole Sammamish upstairs is a full weekend for two people
The saving is the $0.45 line, and the dump fees and your weekend eat most of it

blocks.text: Mistakes that make removal cost more

items: Pulling the carpet but leaving the pad and staples. The slow part is still there, so the tear-out line barely moves.
Ripping out tack strip that was fine. Now it has to be replaced and the subfloor has extra nail holes.
Cutting carpet with a utility knife on a hardwood floor you plan to keep. If there is wood under the carpet, tell us before anyone cuts.
Piling old carpet at the curb. Sammamish curbside pickup does not take it, and most HOAs fine for it.
Painting after tear-out but before install. Staple pulling and stretching scuff fresh base paint.

blocks.title: Where old carpet goes:
blocks.text: Most old Eastside carpet ends up as garbage at a transfer station, because Washington recycling programs for used carpet are limited and depend on fiber type. If yours is a single-fiber nylon, ask at the estimate; sometimes there is an option, often there is not. We would rather say that than promise a green outcome we cannot deliver. For what happens next, see how to prepare for carpet installation.

items.html: Lift a corner in each room. A photo of what is underneath, especially any hardwood or particleboard, changes the plan and the price.
Be honest about pet accidents. Stained subfloor needs sealing before new carpet, and knowing in advance keeps it off the surprise list.
Ask for removal as its own line. Ours is $0.45 per sq ft. If a quote buries tear-out in the total, you cannot compare it against another bid or against doing it yourself.
Check your HOA rules on debris. Klahanie, Trossachs and Sahalee all restrict bins and trailers. Same-day haul-away avoids the issue.
Sequence the trades. Paint before tear-out or after install, not in between. Our carpet installation page explains the full process from tear-out to final vacuum.

faq.q: Is carpet removal included in the price of new carpet?
faq.a: It is its own published line: $0.45 per sq ft for carpet, pad, staples and haul-away, sitting next to the $0.99 per sq ft installation labor on the same firm quote. Other bids sometimes exclude tear-out or leave it vague, so ask before you compare totals.

faq.q: What drives the cost of carpet removal?
faq.a: Floor area sets the published part: $0.45 per sq ft, haul-away included. What sits outside it is glued-down carpet that needs scraping, a pet-damaged subfloor that needs sealing, and tack strip that has to be replaced. Those are quoted as separate lines once we have seen the floor.

faq.q: How long does it take to remove carpet from a whole upstairs?
faq.a: For a typical Sammamish upstairs with three or four bedrooms, a hall and a staircase, tear-out takes our crew a morning, staple pulling and haul-away included. New pad and carpet usually start the same afternoon.

faq.q: Can I dispose of old carpet at the King County transfer station?
faq.a: Yes, as garbage charged by weight, so cut it into rolls you can lift and tape them shut. Sammamish curbside collection does not take carpet, and leaving it at the curb usually draws an HOA notice within a day or two on the plateau.

faq.q: Should I remove the carpet myself to save money?
faq.a: You save the $0.45 per sq ft line, about $653 on a 1,450 sq ft upstairs. To earn it you pull the pad and every staple and haul it to the transfer station, where you pay by weight. Worth it for stretch-in carpet; not for glued or stair carpet.

faq.q: Do you reuse the old tack strip?
faq.a: If it is sound, the right height for the new pad and not rusted, yes. Loose, broken or rusty strip is replaced and priced at the estimate. Never pull tack strip yourself before the estimate; you may be removing something that was fine.
